hills_strategy: The 25 stored firms' filings: operating costs (suppliers and workers) are the largest use of their money; investment, research, buybacks, dividends, taxes and lobbying follow

Jev judged each firm's investment on a scale from pursuing new demand (desire) to defending its position (fear), and which way its money moves it: climb into software/AI, reach down into its own supply, spread across, lean on the state, harvest

hills_mobility: 2015-2025 in the model: among adults 25-54, falls came with a lost job (59% of those who fell), a divorce or separation (22%), discharged debt (9%); climbs with finding work (49%), buying a home (41%), a child (37%), marriage (28%)
2015-2025 in the model, all adults: 33% climbed a fifth or more, 48% stayed in their fifth and 20% fell; the top fifth kept 71% of its members, the bottom fifth 34%

The ladder the view draws (adults 25 and older, ranked within the panel as the tax records rank people): of each fifth's members in 2015, 66% of the top fifth were still there in 2025 (about two in three), 40% of the fourth, 40% of the middle, 48% of the second and 58% of the bottom fifth: about half of the ladder's people stayed in their fifth, and the top kept its members most of all. The US Treasury's 1996-2005 tax-return panel kept 55% of its bottom fifth and 61% of its top fifth
Saving and income from ownership rise with the rung; debt service is highest at the bottom
In the ladder, gold streams are people who climbed a fifth or more, rose streams people who fell, and steel streams people who stayed in their fifth
hills_you: The panel places the viewer by household income and net worth among the year's simulated adults
A dollar of the viewer's spending is split, through the accounts of the industries it buys from, into wages, owners' surplus, taxes, upkeep and imports

For a median household about 85% of all simulated wages and owners' income goes to people ranked above it, weighted by its dollar's split between wages and owners: the population's distribution stands in for where the household's own dollars end up (the model assumes a household's spending pays people the way everyone's does)
The view draws the viewer's own spending as rivers from the viewer to the markets it reaches, split by what is sold out of fear
The cushion is the years of spending the viewer's net worth, home included, would cover; the gold ring at the viewer's feet shows it, one full turn for ten years

Where people like the viewer were ten years later, on a ruler of the income fifths beside the viewer: one step for each fifth that adults in the same income fifth and age band in 2015 had reached by 2025, each ribbon as wide as the share who ended there
Nothing entered in the panel is stored or sent
hills_regimes: General government spending in 2024 (IMF Fiscal Monitor): United States 37.6% of GDP, Sweden 49.2%, China 33.0%, Saudi Arabia 29.2%; the Soviet state budget spent 47.6% of GDP in 1980

atom_mind: Out of reason's gate the mind's choice splits into spending, saving and borrowing, as shares of the year's income; the view draws the three
